fable.w: This section only lists appropriation amounts for conservation programs and how long the funds stay available. It names no outside party (states, tribes, the public, experts) and sets up no consultation, hearing, comment, rulemaking, or right to sue. The only tempting reading is that conservation programs often involve local cooperation, but nothing in this text provides for any such process.

qwen_block.w: This section lists appropriations for various conservation programs. It does not describe any process for consulting with or coordinating with outside parties (such as the public, states, or experts) before making a decision. It is purely a funding authorization.
qwen_block.s: “Conservation operations”, $6,936,000; “Great plains conservation program”, $401,000, to remain available until expended; “Resource conservation and development”, $441,000, to remain available until expended;

opus.w: This section only sets dollar amounts for named conservation accounts and says some funds stay available until spent. It sets up no process for people outside the federal government to take part in a federal decision. Program names alone are not participation, so the label is No.
opus.b: The only thing that might look like participation here is the program names "Conservation operations" and "Resource conservation and development," since conservation programs often involve local partners. That reading fails. This text just lists appropriation amounts. It does not require or allow any consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, or right to sue involving anyone outside the federal government.

qwen_chat.w: This section is an appropriations clause that lists specific dollar amounts authorized for various conservation programs. It does not establish any mechanism for consultation, coordination, or participation by non-federal entities in decision-making. The text merely allocates funds without prescribing any procedural requirements for external input.
qwen_chat.s: “Conservation operations”, $6,936,000; “Great plains conservation program”, $401,000, to remain available until expended; “Resource conservation and development”, $441,000, to remain available until expended;
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that "conservation operations" or "resource conservation" implies public involvement or community input. However, the text is purely an appropriations clause listing budget amounts for specific programs. It does not describe any process for consulting with, coordinating with, or receiving input from non-federal entities. It simply authorizes spending.
